title: Commission a multivariable distillation control architecture
physicalPurpose: Regulate both product purities when interaction strength and actuator feasibility vary inside a declared local operating region.
principalTechnique: Four-path identification, RGA pairing, decoupling, directional robustness, feasibility, and architecture selection
objective: Identify all four local paths and select an unapplied direct, statically decoupled, or centrally constrained architecture from common nominal, interaction, constraint, and abnormal evidence.

simplifications: The declared uncertainty set contains two qualified local linear models and does not represent every distillation condition.
The stronger-interaction model changes only declared cross gains and response times while retaining stable diagonal paths.
The centralized candidate coordinates a static inverse under input limits; it is not MPC and has no optimizer or prediction horizon.
The controllers and allocation execute in Structured Text; singular values, sensitivity, metrics, and selection remain evidence calculations.
Simulation-only I/O and evidence; no physical column or actuator is operated.

baseline.limitation: The identified diagonal pairing and separate PI loops do not by themselves prove weak-direction robustness, interaction uncertainty, or joint input feasibility.

change.decision: Select static decoupling only after four-path identification, RGA pairing and common robustness evidence; retain direct feedback as invalid-mapping fallback and the +2/+2 record as Infeasible.

disturbances: Run separately restored overhead-only, bottoms-only, simultaneous +1/+1, and feed-composition records on each model and architecture.
Run a separately restored +2/+2 stronger-interaction constraint challenge for every architecture.
Do not retune from validation data or include the deliberately infeasible record in normal-envelope ranking.

acceptance.window: mean over the final 10 seconds of each 240-second normal event
complete normal event across both applied inputs
mean over the final 10 seconds of an at-most-300-second restoration interval
0.002 through 2 radians per second over both models and output directions
cross-product residual from requested and applied reflux/reboiler vectors at every limited sample of the +2/+2 challenge

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, invalid, missing, or bound to the wrong model.
Either applied input leaves -10 through +10 percentage points or either product deviation leaves -6 through +6 composition percentage points.
The selected decoupled path is unqualified or controller settings differ between architecture records.
Authority, timing, seed, event, uncertainty case, metric window, or restoration differs across compared records.
safety.restorationMode: Return both setpoint deviations and the feed-disturbance request to zero, transfer both controllers to reviewed Manual authority with explicit zero manual outputs, verify rate-limited inputs and both products restore, and freshly initialize controller state before a new record.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer with the responsible distillation operations and process-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical distillation column, reflux valve, or reboiler-steam valve is operated.
Passing the two-model set does not qualify an untested physical operating condition.
Physical use requires independently reviewed models, topology, product and equipment limits, uncertainty set, abort/restoration, and explicit immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Identify a coupled column, select pairing, test weak directions and constraints, and defend the simplest eligible unapplied architecture.

learning.context: A continuous binary column is identified and evaluated over nominal and stronger-interaction local models with unchanged controllers and physical limits.
learning.reason: A single-loop architecture cannot represent two valves affecting two products, while nominal decoupling and separate loop checks do not prove behavior in weak combined directions or under joint constraints.
theory: Four independently excited paths form the local dynamic matrix.
The Relative Gain Array selects a local steady pairing but does not prove dynamic robustness.
Singular values measure the strongest and weakest directional gains.
Condition number and inverse amplification expose sensitivity to interaction error.
The sensitivity matrix must be checked over direction and frequency.
A central common scale preserves command direction but cannot create unavailable actuator capacity.
learning.workedPrediction: Nominal RGA supports diagonal pairing; the stronger-interaction model needs about 5.44/5.24 input points for a feasible +1/+1 target and about 10.88/10.47 for an infeasible +2/+2 target.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation identity, both model revisions, authority, quality, availability, SP/PV pairs, virtual/requested/applied commands, scale, timing, limits, revision and restoration.
Define identification validity, RGA, singular values, sensitivity, error, interaction, effort, saturation, feasibility, and selection rules before results.
learning.baseline: Identify all four paths, select diagonal pairing, and run direct decentralized PI over the complete common record set rather than inferring robustness from separate loops.
learning.change: Insert the fixed nominal inverse, then add only joint direction-preserving scaling without changing the PI settings.
learning.comparison: Use restored overhead, bottoms, common, load, and infeasible records on the nominal and stronger-interaction models.
learning.validation: Select the least centralized candidate that passes every eligible normal record; classify the +2/+2 challenge as Infeasible.
learning.explanation: Opposing actuator effects create a weak direction, model mismatch raises inverse sensitivity, and allocation cannot overcome physical capacity.
learning.transfer: Use coupled evidence for architecture decisions; Lesson 83 tests whether future coupled constraints justify actual predictive optimization.
